t: Merv grew from a prehistoric oasis settlement into a satrapal centre under the Achaemenid Empire, and was then ruled in turn by Hellenistic kings, Parthians, Sasanians, Arabs, Tahirids, Ghaznavids and Seljuqs.

Abu Muslim declared the Abbasid dynasty at Merv in 748, the caliph al-Ma'mun lived there from 813 to 818, and under the Seljuqs the city reached its greatest size and became the capital of the whole empire from 1118.
The Mongols took the city in 1221 with great loss of life, it never regained its former prosperity, and in 1788 and 1789 Shah Murad of Bukhara razed it and deported its people.
dyk: Merv may have been the largest city in the world in the 12th and 13th centuries, with a population of up to 500,000; Tertius Chandler gave it 200,000 by 1150.
ev: The first city of Merv is founded as part of the Achaemenid expansion under Cyrus the Great
The Seleucid ruler Antiochus Soter renames the city Antiochia Margiana and rebuilds it at Gyaur Gala
The Sasanian Ardashir I takes Merv, beginning almost four centuries of Sasanian rule
Ziyad ibn Abi Sufyan sends 50,000 Arab troops to Merv as a garrison
Abu Muslim declares the new Abbasid dynasty at Merv
The Seljuq Turkmens under Tughril take over Merv peacefully
Merv opens its gates to Tolui, son of Genghis Khan, and most of its people are killed
Shah Murad of Bukhara razes the city and deports its population

f.founded: The first city of Merv was founded in the 6th century BCE as part of the Achaemenid expansion under Cyrus the Great; archaeological surveys show village life on the site from the 3rd millennium BCE.
f.where: In the inland delta of the Murghab river on the southern edge of the Karakum Desert, about 30 km east of the city of Mary in Turkmenistan.
f.known: The capital of the Achaemenid satrapy of Margiana; the base of the Abbasid Revolution of 746 to 750; the residence of the caliph al-Ma'mun from 813 to 818; the capital of the Great Seljuk Empire; its libraries and scholars; the Mongol capture of 1221; the Tomb of Ahmad Sanjar
f.today: The site is preserved by the government of Turkmenistan as the State Historical and Cultural Park Ancient Merv, established in 1987, and is listed by UNESCO as a World Heritage Site.
